company_items.summary: AutoZone reported FQ4 EPS of $56.05 vs. the Street's $54.03, but the beat was low quality — driven by a 145 basis point tariff refund tailwind and a 105 basis point non-cash LIFO boost to gross margins. Domestic comps missed badly at +1.6% vs. +3.1% expected, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management noted improving sales linearity in the back half of the quarter and expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027.

Cognex announced the acquisition of RealSense, described as the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional ~$106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80–90 million in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth. The deal positions Cognex as a stronger player in the fast-growing Physical AI and robotics perception space.

MillerKnoll beat FQ1 EPS estimates with 53 cents vs. the Street's 36 cents, and notably would have still beaten even stripping out an 11-cent tariff refund tailwind, implying underlying EPS of 42 cents. Sales missed, declining 3.3% organically to $923.4 million vs. the $943.2 million consensus, though orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Full-year fiscal 2027 sales guidance was trimmed slightly while the EPS range was left unchanged, and the FQ2 EPS midpoint of 46 cents is in line with consensus.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO effective November 1, with current interim CFO Bob Fishman staying on through the transition. Hau brings prior CFO experience at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. The move brings a seasoned executive into the role and signals a stabilization of leadership.

THOR Industries missed FQ4 EPS at 78 cents vs. the Street's 87 cents, with gross margins falling 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% against an expected 13.85%, as management cited stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflationary pressure on household budgets. Revenue of $2.311 billion came in above the $2.17 billion estimate but that wasn't enough to offset margin weakness. Bright spots included healthy dealer inventory levels, ongoing structural cost actions, and a roughly 75% year-over-year surge in the North American towable RV order backlog, though the company declined to provide formal fiscal 2027 guidance until later in the fall.

Viking Therapeutics shares spiked in pre-market trading after reporting positive trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss in the study. This is a significant clinical readout that validates VK2735 as a competitive asset in the increasingly crowded but high-value GLP-1 obesity drug market. The result materially de-risks the pipeline and could attract partnership or deal interest.

tts_summary:
Good morning. This is a company-specific earnings note for Tuesday, September 22nd, covering six names reporting before the open. No broad macro or Fed commentary in this edition — let's go straight to the movers.

Starting with AutoZone. The company beat on earnings per share, coming in at fifty-six dollars and five cents versus the Street's fifty-four dollars and three cents. But don't get too excited — the quality of that beat is suspect. The upside was driven largely by tariff refunds, which provided a 145 basis point tailwind to gross margins, plus a non-cash LIFO accounting benefit worth another 105 basis points. Strip those out and the picture looks a lot less impressive. Domestic comps missed badly — up just 1.6% versus the 3.1% the Street was looking for — and operating expenses worsened. Management did say sales accelerated in the back half of the quarter and they feel well positioned heading into fiscal 2027, but this is a mixed print at best.

Next, Cognex is buying RealSense — the market leader in depth-sensing cameras for robotic perception and Physical AI — for roughly five hundred million dollars upfront, plus another hundred and six and a half million. RealSense is expected to generate eighty to ninety million dollars in revenue, growing more than fifty percent year over year. This is a strategic move into the Physical AI and robotics space that could meaningfully expand Cognex's addressable market.

MillerKnoll beat estimates with fifty-three cents versus the thirty-six cents expected, and the quality here is better than AutoZone — even backing out an eleven-cent tariff refund, they still would have beaten. Sales missed at nine-twenty-three versus nine-forty-three expected, but orders were up 3.5% year over year. Guidance on the sales line was trimmed slightly, though EPS guidance was left unchanged. Call it a solid, if not spectacular, print.

THOR Industries missed. Earnings came in at seventy-eight cents versus eighty-seven cents expected, with gross margins falling 230 basis points year over year. Management's commentary was cautious, citing interest rates, fuel costs, and inflation squeezing consumers. They're not providing formal fiscal 2027 guidance yet. That said, dealer inventory is healthy, the North American towable RV order backlog surged roughly 75% year over year, and they're taking structural cost actions they say will durably improve margins. Mixed story, leaning slightly negative.

Pentair named a new CFO — Bob Hau, who previously held the role at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox. He takes over November first. Orderly transition, experienced hire.

Finally, the big mover of the morning — Viking Therapeutics. Shares are spiking pre-market after the company reported positive phase results for its GLP-1 drug, showing 22% weight loss. That is a headline number that will get attention. This validates Viking as a serious competitor in the obesity drug space and could draw significant investor and partnership interest.

Bottom line for the session: Viking is the momentum name to watch. AutoZone's beat is likely to face skepticism given the quality issues. THOR's cautious macro read on the consumer is worth flagging for broader sentiment. No index or Fed catalysts in this note, so price action will be stock-driven today.
